data.cultural_impact: Phalgun holds significant cultural significance in various aspects of Hindu society. Throughout India, the starting of the month of Phalgun marks the onset of spring, signifying the rebirth of nature. It is an auspicious time, and numerous Hindu festivals, such as Holi and Mahashivratri, are celebrated during this month. Phalgun is also associated with various deities, like Lord Rama, Cita, Kanha, and Shiva, further emphasizing its importance in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Phalgun represents the essence of transformation and renewal. As the name signifies the arrival of spring, it is associated with the concept of renewal and rejuvenation. On a spiritual level, Phalgun encourages individuals to let go of old habits and make a transformation towards positivity and spiritual growth. The fiery and intense energy of Agni, the god of fire and the presiding deity of this month, is believed to stimulate creativity and passion to manifest one's essence and destiny.

historical_references.reference: Phalgun is the name of the Hindu lunar month corresponding to February–March in the Gregorian calendar.
historical_references.context: Phalgun is the sixth month of the Hindu calendar.

It also represents the triumph of righteousness over adversity, as the month is associated with Lord Hanuman's victory over the demon king Mahiravana.
